knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly assigns response and explanatory roles in a regression modelling question?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the statement that names Y, X, and an actuarial pair.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Y is the outcome for the modelling question; X variables are predictors with a warrant. Putting every numeric column on the right-hand side, or treating claim count as automatically an X for severity, ignores the modelling question.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Response is the outcome modelled; explanatory variables are predictors. Example: claim severity (Y) vs age and sum insured.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Column-soup modelling, or treating claim count as automatically an explanatory variable for severity.

choices.label: The response variable Y is the outcome being modelled or predicted; explanatory variables X are the predictors thought to help explain or predict Y. Example: claim severity (Y) with age and sum insured as X variables.
Every numeric column in a data set is automatically an explanatory variable; the response is whichever column has the largest variance.
Claim count is always an explanatory variable when modelling claim severity, because both are numeric policy fields.
Response and explanatory roles are defined only after writing a simple versus multiple linear model equation; variable roles cannot be stated before model form.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Motor book: you want to model claim severity. Columns include age, sum insured, claim amount, NCD discount, and claim count. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Name Y and warranted X variables; refuse column-soup.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: For severity modelling, claim amount is Y. Age and sum insured are plausible X's with warrants. Claim count is a different outcome type. Column-soup is not role assignment.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Y = claim amount (severity). X examples: age, sum insured. Refuse column-soup.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting column-soup or treating claim count as automatically an X for severity.

choices.label: Response Y = claim amount (severity, the outcome to explain). Explanatory examples: age and sum insured (predictors of severity with a one-sentence warrant each). Claim count is a frequency outcome, not automatically an X for severity. Putting every numeric column on the right-hand side is not variable-role modelling.
Response Y = claim count; explanatory variables are claim amount, age, sum insured, and NCD because all numeric columns belong on the right-hand side.
Response Y = claim amount; claim count must also be an explanatory variable because it appears in the same policy record as severity.
No response can be named until a multiple regression equation is fully written; severity modelling starts with equation form, not Y versus X.

worked_example.title: Assign Y and X, then evaluate a severity line
worked_example.problem_statement: A motor pricing analyst models claim severity (£). The fitted simple linear relationship from a pilot sample is ŷ = 1200 + 40x, where x is driver age in years. (a) Name the response and the explanatory variable. (b) Compute the fitted mean severity at age 45.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Name Y and X in one sentence, then substitute x = 45 into ŷ.

steps.label: Assign response and explanatory roles
steps.attempt_cue: State which quantity is Y and which is X.
steps.explanation: The modelling question is claim severity, so severity is the response Y. Age is the predictor used to explain severity, so age is the explanatory variable X.
steps.calculation: Y = claim severity (£); X = driver age (years)

steps.label: Evaluate the fitted mean at age 45
steps.explanation: Once roles are fixed, the fitted line gives the modelled mean response at a chosen X value.

steps.label: Refuse column-soup
steps.attempt_cue: State why claim count is not automatically an X for severity.
steps.explanation: Claim count is a frequency outcome. Sharing a policy record with severity does not make it an automatic explanatory variable for a severity model.
steps.calculation: Claim count is a different outcome type, not auto-X for severity
steps.result: Roles fixed by the modelling question, not by column presence

worked_example.final_answer: Y = claim severity, X = driver age; ŷ(45) = £3000. Claim count is not automatically an explanatory variable for severity.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Treating every numeric policy field (including claim count) as an explanatory variable for severity, or swapping roles so that age is modelled as Y and severity as X.
